payload.markdown: Between them, the classes in the Reflection API provide unprecedented runtime access to information about the objects, functions, and extensions in your scripts.

blocks.text: Between them, the classes in the Reflection API provide unprecedented runtime access to information about the objects, functions, and extensions in your scripts.

payload.markdown: The Reflection API’s power and reach mean you should usually use it in preference to the class and object functions. You will soon find it indispensable as a tool for testing classes. You might want to generate class diagrams or documentation, for example, or you might want to save object information to a database, examining an object’s accessor (getter and setter) methods to extract field names. Building a framework that invokes methods in module classes according to a naming scheme is another use of Reflection.

items: Classes & Objects: A class defines state and behaviour; objects are instances of that definition.
Constants: Immutable named values declared with const or define().
Functions: Reusable blocks of code that take arguments and return values.
HTTP & REST: Designing HTTP endpoints as resources with predictable methods and status codes.
Properties & Methods: Class state held in properties, and behaviour implemented as methods.
Reflection: Inspecting classes, methods and properties from running code.
Return Types: The declared type of a function's return value.
Static & Constants: Members belonging to the class itself rather than to any one instance.
